sources.entry: MenuBarMijia - Control Xiaomi Mi Home devices from the menu bar by voice or keyboard, via Mi Cloud QR login or Home Assistant (macOS 26+). [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jryang1997/MenuBarMijia) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu-bar controller for Xiaomi Mi Home (Mijia) and Home Assistant devices, with voice, keyboard search, and a companion Windows 11 tray app.
summary.what_it_does: MenuBarMijia puts smart-home controls in the macOS menu bar. You can search devices by name, room, or Pinyin initials and toggle them from the keyboard (⌥M opens the panel). Holding the menu-bar icon records a spoken command that is sent across multiple devices, and a local parser handles clear commands while optional AI models handle complex ones. It connects to Mi Cloud via a QR code scan in Mi Home, or to a Home Assistant instance over a long-lived token and LAN WebSocket. Features include undo for batch changes, timers, All Off, safety alerts, nine visual skins, custom groups, Shortcuts actions, and Mac event triggers such as Away and Back. A separate Tauri-based Windows 11 tray app supports Mi Cloud login and demo mode but not Home Assistant or voice.
use_cases: Control smart lights, fans, and air conditioners from the Mac menu bar
Turn off study lights when leaving the Mac
Give voice commands to change several smart devices at once
Search and toggle Mi Home devices from the keyboard
Run Home Assistant entities in a Mac menu-bar panel
Track smart plug energy use on a Mac
notable: Hold-to-speak voice control from the menu bar, with no wake word and no spoken reply
Mi Cloud QR-code login plus Home Assistant backend, merging HA entities into one card per device
Undo bar that restores brightness, color temperature, light mode, and climate setpoints
Mac automation triggers (Away, Back, external display) and four macOS Shortcuts actions
Credentials stored in the macOS Keychain, with an explicit cloud-AI consent step
caveats: macOS 14 or later required; the Mac build is Apple Silicon only per the release notes, and the release is self-signed and not Apple-notarized, so Gatekeeper may block it on first launch
Mi Cloud uses Xiaomi's undocumented private API, and commands pass through Xiaomi's servers; Xiaomi has restricted unofficial clients in the past
Windows app lacks Home Assistant, menu-bar speech, safety alerts, and feature parity with the Mac app; Windows installers ship unsigned in 1.1.0
